2p_vector.notes: Trained with max^n MCTS (= negamax at N=2), 30 iterations, augmentation + gamma=0.99. 40/40 vs the greedy racer at 200 sims (20 games/seat), winning both seats — including seat 0, which cannot be won by racing (two racers meet head-on and the second jumps the first, so seat 0 must spend a wall). Uses walls in both seats, ~38-43% of turns. The strongest model in the repo. Its gamma=0.97 sibling (runs/n2_5x5_g097_v1) scores 20/40 — same seat 1, but 0/20 in seat 0, because the steeper discount suppresses paying a tempo now for a win later.

4p_ship.notes: Trained with max^n MCTS, 70 iterations, augmentation + γ=0.99. Peak checkpoint iter 68.

2p_legacy.notes: Original scalar architecture. Trained with negamax MCTS, v3.2 notebook, 40 iterations.

2p_9x9.eval_win_rate: ~97-100% vs random (fair share 50%) BUT 0% vs a greedy pawn-rush
2p_9x9.notes: Full-size 9x9, 10 walls/player. max^n MCTS, 600 sims, gamma=0.99. best.pt = accept-gated peak of n2_9x9_v4. NOT DEMO-READY: 0/40 vs the greedy racer on every one of 12 training evals, and 0/12 on a direct per-seat probe at 200 sims (seat 0 and seat 1 both). It spends ~61% of its turns placing walls and loses even the seat where walking forward wins outright. The vs-random number is saturated and hides this — do not quote it alone.

4p_9x9.eval_win_rate: ~88-96% vs random (fair share 25%) BUT 0% vs a greedy pawn-rush
4p_9x9.notes: Full-size 9x9, 5 walls/player. max^n MCTS, 600 sims, gamma=0.99. best.pt = accept-gated peak of n4_9x9_v5. NOT DEMO-READY: 0/40 vs the greedy racer on all 14 training evals. Same pathology as 2p_9x9. The vs-random number is saturated — do not quote it alone.
